overview: Software engineering produces its own data: commits, reviews, builds, tests, incidents and tickets. Quality shows up late and noisily, developers are sensitive to being measured and code, secrets and customer data are among a company's most confidential assets, so tools assist engineers inside sandboxes and leave merges and releases to people.

concepts.name: Code review is a quality gate and a learning channel
concepts.explanation: Reviewers catch defects, share knowledge and keep designs consistent. Their time is limited, so tools that point to risky changes or likely issues help most when they cite evidence and leave the decision to the reviewer.
concepts.whyItMatters: Tools that comment on everything teach reviewers to ignore them.

concepts.name: Tests are slow, flaky and unevenly useful
concepts.explanation: Large suites take hours and some tests fail without a code cause. Selecting and ordering tests by their chance of catching a regression saves time, but only if flaky tests are separated from real failures.
concepts.whyItMatters: Skipping tests to save time moves risk to production.

concepts.name: Pipelines fail for many reasons
concepts.explanation: A broken build can come from code, dependencies, infrastructure or configuration. Finding the first real error in a long log, and linking it to recent changes, cuts the time to fix.
concepts.whyItMatters: A diagnosis that does not show its evidence is hard to trust.

concepts.name: Deployments carry risk that can be staged
concepts.explanation: Canaries, progressive rollouts and feature flags limit the damage of a bad release. The risk depends on change size, service criticality and timing.
concepts.whyItMatters: Gating decisions should be policy with model input and not a model alone.

concepts.name: Application security depends on reachability
concepts.explanation: Scanners report many findings, but only some are reachable and exploitable in a given application. Prioritising by reachability, exposure and data sensitivity focuses scarce fixing time.
concepts.whyItMatters: A raw severity score floods teams with findings that cannot be exploited.

concepts.name: The software supply chain is an attack surface
concepts.explanation: Packages, build tools and CI systems are used to deliver malicious code. Controls include provenance, signed builds, dependency pinning and registry proxies.
concepts.whyItMatters: One compromised package can reach every build that installs it.

concepts.name: Developer productivity is a team-level concept
concepts.explanation: Flow metrics such as lead time and deployment frequency describe a system. Used on individuals, they are gamed and harm trust.
concepts.whyItMatters: Any measurement should be aggregated to teams and agreed with employee representatives where required.

concepts.name: Coding agents act with the permissions you give them
concepts.explanation: Agents that read repositories and run commands can be steered by hostile text in files, issues and web pages. They need sandboxes, short-lived scoped credentials, egress limits and human approval for risky actions.
concepts.whyItMatters: Controls belong in the platform, not in prompt instructions that an attacker can override.
